strengths: Overall the manuscript reads quite coherently.
The author’s proposition of defining constraints as opposed to target specifications is an interesting approach for addressing design problems.
By having fewer specifications, it seems plausible the authors framework could offer nove alternatives for addressing a number of hard problems.

The meta-specification approach presents a unique perspective on OELS, shifting from an explicit to an implicit design, which could simplify design complexity while expanding the space of possibilities.
The paper formalizes a unified framework for OELS, creating a common language that facilitates the comparison of different OELS approaches.

The implementation of co-evolving robotic agents and tasks showcases the potential of meta specification and watchmaker functions to create emergent behaviors without requiring highly specific design constraints.
The use of LLM-based watchmaker functions offer a promising approach for larger-scale OELS implementations.
The strength of the paper is that it offers a practical solution to a significant scaling problem in open-ended learning systems.
Open-endedness is an important subject that deserves more attention.

The experiments, although minimal, seem to point towards some novelty (I am not aware of any experiment co-evolving both tasks and agents, in a 3D world, with language descriptions and LLM-based evolution operators) and hint at potentially interesting future work.
The paper is very well written, both in terms of content and of the very pretty presentation.
weaknesses: Plagiarism of existing ideas, see Details Of Ethics Concerns section

The contributions of the paper could be made clearer; compared to POET, can the proposed system solve anything that POET cannot or is it mostly just a generalized formulation of a class of algorithms.

The paper does not really show any open ended learning; the authors omitted any training procedure, which is crucial for the evolved robots to become increasingly capable, and a control mechanism should be integrated to ensure continuous progress.
Typo: “representation sapce” in the watchmaker function definition
The main contribution of the paper is unclear; it may only add feasibility checks rather than a substantial novel contribution.
The term "watchmaker functions" appears superfluous because similar filtering steps exist in prior work (e.g., Karl Sims' virtual creatures and Lehman et al.).
The formal specification of the OELS framework is confusing; it's not clear what components belong to evolution functions versus the control system.
The description of POET conflates control mechanism with environment evolution function, leading to confusion.
The experiments closely resemble those of Faldor et al. 2024, yet the paper fails to cite this prior work.
In line 334, "generalized transformation" should read "viability" to match terminology.
